newsitem.title: MEXICO: Vitro to offer medium-term notes.
newsitem.headline: Vitro to offer medium-term notes.

text.p: Mexican glass-maker Vitro SA said on Monday it would offer medium-term notes denominated in inflation-indexed UDI units worth about 515 million pesos.
The company will offer 305,859,400 UDIs, which at Monday's price of 1.68378 pesos equals about 515 million pesos.
The offer began on Monday and will close on Tuesday.
The notes mature on December 7, 1999 and will offer a fixed real interest rate of 13 percent. Duff and Phelps rated the notes MAA-, according to Vitro.
Sources close to the deal, who asked not to be identified, said the money will be used to restructure debt at the company, which recently sold off its troubled U.S. unit Anchor Glass Corp.
The local lead manager will be Valores Finamex Brokerage firm, with Inverlat Brokerage as the syndicated manager, Vitro said.
